newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Sihanouk rejects autonomy for Khmer Rouge defectors.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk rejects autonomy for Khmer Rouge defectors.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk vowed to oppose any bid by Khmer Rouge dissident Ieng Sary and his followers to carve out an autonomous zone in the country's northwest.
"The demands of Mr Ieng Sary and his 'Generals' are unacceptable," the king said in a written response to questions posed by the Cambodia Daily newspaper and published on Wednesday.

"I dare say I would reject a proposed royal decree if ever this proposal, emanating from our two prime ministers (Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen), offered Mr Ieng Sary and his group an autonomous zone," Sihanouk added.
"No territorial autonomy whatsoever within Cambodia can be tolerated," he said, adding that the royal government must be the chief authority throughout the nation.

Guerrilla commanders loyal to breakaway Khmer Rouge official Ieng Sary, foreign minister during the brutal 1975-79 Khmer Rouge rule, told government peace negotiators last month they wanted the Pailin area to become a new province under their control.

Ieng Sary and his fighters around the strongholds of Pailin and Phnom Malai broke with Khmer Rouge hardliners loyal to rebel leader Pol Pot in August. The dissidents last month began talks on merging their forces with government troops after the king granted a royal amnesty to Ieng Sary for his alleged role in Khmer Rouge atrocities.
Ieng Sary and Pol Pot were sentenced to death in absentia for their roles in the genocide of more than one million people during the Khmer Rouge reign of terror.

First Prime Minister Ranariddh has said he does not oppose creating a new province around Pailin, an area rich in gems in timber, but both he and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen have stressed that all areas must come under government control.

Sihanouk said the resources in Khmer Rouge areas such as Pailin, Phnom Malai and Anlong Veng in the north "belong exclusively to the people of Cambodia and not to the Khmer Rouge, ex-Khmer Rouge or other individuals, groups, etc."

The king, who was held a virtual hostage in his palace for much of the Khmer Rouge's time in power, told the Cambodia Daily he personally opposed amnesty for Ieng Sary but had decided to pardon him at the request of the co-premiers and a majority of the 120 members of parliament.
"I must bow before those who 'weigh heavily' on the decisions of a constitutional monarch who 'reigns but does not govern,'" his written statement said.
The Khmer Rouge signed a U.N.-brokered peace treaty with rival Cambodian factions in 1991 but later reneged on the pact and has been fighting the coalition government formed after 1993 elections.
